findings.claim: The resilience limits are checked on the raw input, not on the validated copy. A getter or Proxy on the passed object can therefore get past the 12-candidate limit (and v2's 16), the 1..7 case limit and the 'at least 1 exclusion' rule; optimizeResilience then reports status 'optimal'. Cause: validateResilience reads plan.candidates.length (line 42) and then calls PL.validatePlanScenario. That function reads input.candidates again and checks cands.length before cands.map (plan.js lines 81/92). The same happens with cases.length (line 47) before cases.map (line 50), and with ids.length (line 63) before iterating. The lengths of cleanPlan.candidates, clean (cases) and set.size are never re-checked. This cannot be reached through JSON import, because parsed objects are plain. It breaks the spec rule that 'Непроверенные объекты при прямом вызове публичных evaluate/optimize/создания поиска валидировать... изменение переданного объекта не должно обходить ограничения'. It also breaks the limits 'Полный перебор <=4096' and 1..7 cases. Fix: snapshot each array once (Array.from), or re-check the clean lengths before returning; the same fix is needed in plan.js validatePlanScenario.

findings.claim: The JSON round trip fails for a label that contains U+FFFD. validateResilience accepts it; importResilience also accepts it when the file writes it as the escape �. exportResilience then writes the character raw, because JSON.stringify does not escape it. X.parseStrict rejects any raw U+FFFD as bad_encoding, so the module cannot re-import its own export. The label is the only free-text field, since v2 IDs cannot contain U+FFFD. Fix: reject U+FFFD in labels, or escape it on export.

findings.claim: Results and explanations are not tied to the scenario that produced them, so a late answer from an earlier scenario cannot be detected. The output of evaluateResilience has no digest or request_id. optimizeResilience returns resilience_problem_digest=null unless opts.F is passed. explainResilience(env, manual, result) checks nothing: it accepts a manual plan or result computed for a different envelope and writes mixed text. For example, it names envelope B's duplicate group k0=k1 but lists only 'k0' as worst, taken from envelope A's result. v2's explainPlans rejects this case with stale_explanation. Marked plausible: the UI (BUILD stage 3) might add a guard, but the module API has no way to do this check.

findings.claim: The label check rejects only C0, DEL, C1 and U+2028/2029. It accepts a label made only of invisible U+200B, because trim() does not remove it, so 'непустая' is met only formally. It accepts Bidi_Control format characters such as U+202E RLO, which can visually reverse the rest of the label when shown as text. It also accepts lone surrogates, which are not Unicode scalar values and cannot be encoded in UTF-8; any UTF-8 writer, such as an HTML report or a Python oracle using ensure_ascii=False, would replace or reject them. Whether this is a spec deviation depends on the reading: whether 'управляющие символы' covers only Cc or also Bidi_Control.

checked_ok: Read resilience.js (230 lines) and plan.js (426 lines) in full, plus whatif.parseStrict. The product test tests/resilience.cjs passes in the snapshot ('all resilience checks passed').

Strict envelope: unknown top-level field -> unknown_field (including derived names such as nominal and results); plan.derived_results -> derived_not_allowed; extra case field -> bad_shape; missing schema_version, plan or cases -> missing_field; schema_version null or unknown -> bad_version; v2 or v1 file -> wrong_version; an own __proto__ key at top level or in a case is rejected.

Candidate limit: 13 candidates -> too_many_candidates from validate, evaluate, createSearch, optimize and export, before precomputation, even when the plan is also otherwise invalid (foreign snapshot). 12 are accepted, and v2 optimizePlans still solves 13 to 16.

Cases: 0 or 8 -> bad_cases; 7 accepted; 'base' -> reserved_id (exact match, so 'Base' is allowed); duplicate case ID -> duplicate_id; ID rules follow PL.isId (NFC, Kazakh letters, 64 code points, empty, number, non-NFC).
Labels: 120 emoji (240 UTF-16 units) accepted, 121 rejected; empty, spaces only or NBSP only rejected; TAB, LF, DEL, NEL (U+0085) and U+2028 rejected; non-string rejected; markup kept as plain text.

disabled_source_ids: empty -> bad_exclusions; all 15 records accepted; 16 -> bad_exclusions; duplicate -> duplicate_id; candidate ID -> candidate_not_source; ID of another category, another city or a case-variant -> unknown_source; non-string -> bad_id; non-array or null -> bad_shape. A candidate whose ID equals a source ID is treated in the source namespace.
Plain mutation of the caller's envelope after createResilienceSearch (more candidates, empty cases, max_selected 99, budget 1e9) does not affect the result: the search runs on the validated copy.

Randomized differential test, 400 runs, both cities and both categories, 0..9 candidates, duplicate candidate positions, required and excluded IDs, cases that disable all records, duplicate cases, run against my own independent brute force with its own haversine, mm rounding and feasibility: 0 mismatches in status, nominal IDs, robust IDs, robust W, worst_case_ids for nominal and robust (141 runs had tied worst cases), feasible_count and price.
Nominal plan equals plan.js optimizePlans objectives.mean.ids in all 400 runs.
Robust objective (W, L_base, cost, sorted IDs) matches the brute force; W is the lexicographic maximum over all cases including base, and is never a mix of components from different cases.

Per-case manual evaluation, 200 runs: before/after/delta, nearest_after kind and ID, unknown_count, weighted_sum_mm, max_mm (null when unknown), covered_weight, weighted_mean_mm, source_records and disabled_count all match my own computation for every case.

Order independence, 200 runs, with cases, exclusion IDs, control points, candidates and selected_ids shuffled: identical problem digest, exclusions digest, scenario digest, nominal and robust IDs, worst vectors and IDs, price and feasible_count. selected_ids enters only the scenario digest; the problem digest changes when a duplicate case is added.

Duplicate cases leave nominal, robust, W and price unchanged; worst_case_ids lists both duplicates when that case is worst; duplicate_case_groups shows the duplicates (the order of the groups follows input order, which is cosmetic only).

When all records are disabled and no candidates are selected: per-case distance, mean and max are null, delta is null, coverage is 0, and W = (n, 0, null) with that case named. Robust and nominal then select a candidate. No Infinity or NaN appears in the JSON output.

Price is (robust base mean minus nominal base mean)/1000. It is exactly 0 when the plans coincide, and null with a reason when the status is infeasible, cancelled or incomplete. The 'base mean unknown' branch cannot be reached by a valid envelope, because a case needs at least one category record, so base always has a baseline.

Required cost over budget, or more required than max_selected -> status infeasible with reasons, evaluated 0, price null, constraints kept. A manual plan missing a required candidate is flagged missing_required.

Search lifecycle: result() before any step, after step(0), after step(4095 of 4096), after step(NaN, -5 or 'abc'), and after cancel (including cancel after completion) is never 'optimal'. step returns true after cancel; request_id is passed through. Full 12 candidates x 25 points x 8 cases takes about 23 ms.

Export contains only the input (schema_version, plan with the 12 v2 input keys, cases with id, label and sorted exclusions). export -> import -> export is byte-identical. An Astana envelope imports into the Astana context.

Strict import: trailing data, double BOM, duplicate keys (case and plan), NaN, Infinity, -1e400, raw control characters, nesting depth over 32 and a raw U+FFFD are all rejected; 256 KiB + 1 byte -> too_large, exactly 256 KiB accepted; a v1 or v2 file -> wrong_version; a Shymkent plan relabelled as Astana -> foreign_snapshot; unknown city -> bad_city with ctxFor not called. A failed import leaves the context unchanged; the function only returns on success (atomic).
A file without 'plan' is rejected, but with code bad_city instead of missing_field (cosmetic, not reported as a finding).
Context immutability: ctx stays frozen; caseContext returns a filtered copy; result.source_snapshot is the plan's own; the exclusions digest is separate.
Explanation text contains 'не подтверждение закрытия' and no probabilities, risk, population or tenge.
